record.original_question: Does there exist a skew weighing matrix W(18,9), meaning an 18 x 18 matrix with entries in {0,1,-1} such that W W^T = 9I, each row and column has exactly 9 nonzero entries, distinct rows are orthogonal, and the matrix is skew-symmetric (W^T = -W)?

evidence.quote: A "weighing matrix" W(n,w) with parameters (n,w) is an n by n square matrix (n rows and n columns) with entries in {0,1,-1} that satisfies W W^T = wI. That is, W times its transpose is equal to the constant w times the identity matrix I. The weighing matrix will have w nonzero entries in each row and each column. And each pair of distinct rows is orthogonal (dot product zero). Given (n,w), we want to construct "SkewW", a skew weighing matrix W(n,w) that satisfies these properties and is also a skew matrix: that is, W^T = -W.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Does there exist a skew weighing matrix of order 18 and weight 9? Equivalently, does there exist an 18×18 matrix W with entries in {-1, 0, 1} such that:
(i) W W^T = 9 I_{18},
(ii) every row and every column contains exactly 9 nonzero entries,
(iii) any two distinct rows are orthogonal (their Euclidean inner product is 0), and
(iv) W is skew-symmetric, i.e., W^T = -W (so in particular all diagonal entries are 0)?
artifact.status_search_result: A skew weighing matrix W(18,9) is known to exist; explicit constructions of weighing matrices of order 18 and weight 9 (including skew versions) appear in the combinatorial design literature, and this case has been recorded as resolved (existence confirmed).

status_evidence.snippet: Weighing matrices and skew-symmetric variants are studied; existence tables list known constructions for small orders.
status_evidence.claim: General context for existence of weighing matrices including skew-symmetric ones.

status_evidence.title: Group developed weighing matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Group-developed W(18,9) constructions are presented, including disjoint (Z_2 x Z_3 x Z_3)-developed W(18,9).
status_evidence.claim: W(18,9) constructions exist, supporting feasibility of the skew variant.
